title: A Wreck for the Trail
premise: Sable Fairweather, a disgraced mountain guide drifting through the borderlands of Kestria, pulls a sealed chest from a flooded river and finds it stamped with the crest of Vhalen, a nation erased from every map. The chest holds proof that Vhalen's last royal surveyor mapped a high glacier pass before the country fell — and someone is willing to kill to keep that route buried. Hunted by a mercenary archivist and shadowed by Wren, a runaway cartographer's apprentice who becomes an unlikely ally, Sable must survive the monsoon in a leaking boat, cross hostile territory, and reach the pass during the brief calving-season window. In the end, Sable chooses to publish the map rather than sell or destroy it, sacrificing their hard-won anonymity but finally choosing who they are instead of running from who they were.
about_author: Juniper Fairweather is the pen name of a former river guide who spent six seasons leading expeditions through glacial valleys before turning to writing full-time. Their fiction draws on firsthand knowledge of mountain rescue, monsoon travel, and the quiet ethics of people who live off the map.

chapters.title: The River Keeps What It Is Owed
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Working a low-paying ferry run during early monsoon floods, Sable spots a chest snagged in drowned willows and hauls it aboard to sell the brass fittings. Inside: survey plates bearing the seal of dead Vhalen. The beat is wary curiosity — Sable has survived by never touching anything that matters.

chapters.title: Two Countries' Worth of Enemies
chapters.summary: Sable's POV, flashback-woven. We learn why Sable was blacklisted from Kestria and Ondmark: a guided party that died, a report Sable signed under another name. A Kestrian harbor clerk recognizes them. Emotional beat: shame worn as camouflage.

chapters.title: What the Seal Means
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren, a fugitive apprentice cartographer hiding on the same dock, recognizes the Vhalen crest instantly and confronts Sable, offering to decode the plates in exchange for passage upstream. Beat: two liars recognizing each other's craft.

chapters.title: The Man Who Buys Dead Things
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. A soft-spoken buyer named Corvane offers a fortune for the chest unopened. Sable refuses on instinct; that night their boat is searched and their ferry contract burned. Beat: the price of curiosity arrives early.

chapters.title: Leaking
chapters.summary: Sable and Wren's alternating POV. They flee upriver in Sable's aging boat as the monsoon hits full force; the hull begins taking water faster than the pump can manage. Forced intimacy of bailing side by side. Beat: grudging partnership forming under pressure.

chapters.title: The Cartographer's Daughter
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren reveals her father was Vhalen's last royal surveyor and that the plates show a pass he hid inside the glacier survey — a route out of Kestria no government controls. She wants it published; Sable wants it gone. Beat: clashing motives, shared danger.

chapters.title: Corvane's Ledger
chapters.summary: Antagonist POV (Corvane). We see his method: he erases inconvenient geography for paying states, and the Vhalen pass would unravel three border treaties. He dispatches hunters. Beat: cold, patient menace — the reader learns what Sable doesn't.

chapters.title: Salt and Rust
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Repairs at a derelict smelting town; Sable trades a plate fragment for hull patches, keeping the key one hidden even from Wren. A hunter arrives asking questions. Beat: Sable's instinct to hoard trust nearly costs them everything when Wren catches the lie.

chapters.title: The Argument at the Weir
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Cornered at a river weir, Sable and Wren fight openly — about the map, about Sable's past, about whether survival justifies silence. Hunters close in; they escape together anyway. Beat: rupture followed by reluctant honesty.

chapters.title: Monsoon Country
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Days of storm travel; Wren teaches Sable to read her father's cipher while Sable teaches Wren how to read water. A near-drowning forces Sable to save Wren at real risk. Beat: found family forming without either naming it.

chapters.title: The Village That Wasn't on Any Map
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. They shelter with a river community of people who also live unregistered — exiles, deserters, erased families. For one night Sable experiences what staying might feel like. Beat: temptation of belonging, and fear of it.

chapters.title: Paid in Names
chapters.summary: Village elder's POV. The villagers hide the pair but demand payment: Sable must guide their sick children over a local ridge before the flood cuts the trail. Sable guides well — and realizes they still can. Beat: identity beginning to turn from shame toward choice.

chapters.title: Hunters on the Ridge
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Corvane's men catch up during the children's crossing; Sable uses a controlled rockfall to break the pursuit, nearly dying, and loses the decoy chest. Beat: competence reclaimed, cost made visible.

chapters.title: What Sable Signed
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren finally reads the old incident report and understands the deaths weren't Sable's fault — the route was sabotaged, and Sable took the blame to protect a client's family. Beat: forgiveness offered before it's asked for.

chapters.title: The Calving Season Opens
chapters.summary: Dual POV. The glacier begins to calve; the pass window is open for days only. They race the meltwater with Corvane a day behind. Beat: hope sharpened into urgency.

chapters.title: Ice Underfoot
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. The ascent: crevasse fields, a rope team of two, Wren navigating by her father's cipher while Sable leads on instinct. A bridge collapse strands them overnight on an ice shelf. Beat: trust tested at altitude.

chapters.title: Corvane's Offer
chapters.summary: Corvane catches them below the summit col and makes his real pitch: sell the plates, walk away rich and anonymous forever — everything Sable claims to want. Sable hesitates. Beat: the antagonist offers not violence but comfort, which is worse.

chapters.title: The Pass of Vhalen
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Climax: they cross the pass as the glacier calves around them, using the survey plates to find safe line where maps fail. Corvane pursues onto unstable ice and is lost to a serac fall after refusing Sable's offered rope. Beat: survival won by skill and mercy both.

chapters.title: The Other Side
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Beyond the pass lies open, unmapped country — freedom, but also the end of the road that bound them. Wren asks what Sable will do now. Beat: exhaustion, grief, and the first honest conversation between them.

chapters.title: A Name Given Freely
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Instead of vanishing, Sable sends copies of the plates to three newspapers and signs them 'Sable Fairweather, guide.' The blacklist becomes irrelevant next to the story breaking worldwide. Beat: reclaiming identity as an act, not an accident.

chapters.title: Consequences
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Governments react; inquiries reopen the old disaster; some doors close permanently. But the village sends word that its children are safe, and Wren's father's work is recognized posthumously. Beat: the price of survival paid in full, and worth it.

chapters.title: Where the Trail Starts
chapters.summary: Sable's POV, final chapter. Spring: Sable and Wren outfit a new boat and take their first paying clients — refugees using the Vhalen route legally now. Stopping no longer costs more than staying. Beat: quiet resolution; a guide with nothing left to hide, a family chosen, a map that outlived its nation.
